subject.title: Rename i18n locale codes from region-based (zh-CN/zh-TW) to script-based (zh-Hans/zh-Hant)

question: Should OpenClaw make `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` the canonical stored and public Chinese locale IDs, or keep shipped `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` as canonical while only normalizing script-style inputs to them?
rationale: Both directions are technically possible, but the choice changes a shipped public locale surface and saved user preference behavior; repository policy requires explicit migration/fallback intent rather than an automatic rename.

options.title: Keep current canonical IDs
options.body: Leave `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` as stored/public IDs and, if needed, add or document script-tag input normalization without changing saved values.

options.title: Switch to script IDs with migration
options.body: Rename the runtime, generator, docs, tests, and saved browser preference handling in one coordinated compatibility-sensitive change.

options.title: Defer to broader localization policy
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers decide the larger locale naming policy across Control UI, CLI wizard, docs publishing, and native app surfaces.

recommendation.title: Keep current canonical IDs
recommendation.body: Leave `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` as stored/public IDs and, if needed, add or document script-tag input normalization without changing saved values.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent i18n/docs ownership signals and broad repository policy context make this the best available routing candidate for the product-direction decision.
